name: NY-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 24 points, among the bluest in New York
Meeks is a well-funded incumbent with $2.1 million on hand; challenger Marsh reports no fundraising
Prediction markets price the Democratic win near 98 percent
No public polls or expert ratings, so the outlook rests on structural fundamentals
model.rationale: A 24-point Democratic district, a longtime incumbent holding a roughly $2.1 million financial edge over a challenger with no reported fundraising, and markets pricing the race near 98 percent Democratic leave little room for doubt; only the size of the win is realistically in question.
model.watch: An unforeseen scandal or a late self-funded challenger surge could narrow the margin, though the district's lean makes an upset highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
New York's fifth district, centered in Queens, leans Democratic by roughly 24 points, and longtime incumbent Gregory Meeks is seeking reelection. He has raised about $2.2 million and holds $2.1 million on hand, while Republican George Marsh reports no fundraising. No public polls cover the race and no expert raters list it, so the outlook rests on the district's strong partisan lean.

Prediction markets put the Democratic chance near 98 percent, matching the structural picture. The national environment could trim the margin a few points, but an upset would require an extraordinary shift. The realistic question is whether Meeks wins by 25 points or closer to 15, not which party carries the seat.
